summary.manuscript_text: Z1 is admissible only if the 48-V current in its package network is smooth. Charge balance asks for 0.56 uF per cell for 1 V of ripple, but a circuit model of the cells' phase-A pulse against the 3.1-mOhm package network leaves k = 2.2 at that value; k <= 1.2 needs about 2.9 uF per cell at 48 V, and the Z1 stack has no room for it (the cell tiers are full and the 0.8-mm gaps take only 0402 parts, at most 4.7 nF at 100 V and 125 C, which resonate with the package inductance). The decoupling is therefore made physical as seven interleaved clock phases over the 7 x 7 cells and a ring of 56 1206 100-V X7S capacitors (65 uF at 48 V and 105 C) outside the cell grid: a 49-cell model of the package sheets gives k = 1.65 (1.63-1.72 over the loop-inductance band), and at the converged S0 temperatures the package-internal loss rises to 149.0 W.
